Strategy: Write the two affine formulas for $x<y$ and $x>y$. Their values agree at $x=y$ and equal zero at the appropriate endpoints. Direct differentiation gives slopes $(b-y)/(b-a)$ and $-(y-a)/(b-a)$, whose right-minus-left jump is $-1$. Integrating by parts separately on $(a,y)$ and $(y,b)$ against a compact test function proves the Dirac identity. Swapping $x,y$ leaves the min/max formula unchanged; subtracting the one-dimensional fundamental kernel cancels the slope jump and leaves a globally affine harmonic corrector.
